phases.title: Execution, claims, and discrete structure
phases.premise: Before a system can be designed or optimized, model state and make claims precise enough to prove or refute.
phases.gate: Defend one invariant, repair one flawed proof, construct a smallest counterexample, and name the cost model of the check.

phases.title: Representation and algorithmic strategy
phases.premise: A representation decides which operations are cheap, which invariants are local, and which strategy the structure permits.
phases.gate: Read an unfamiliar data-structure implementation, recover its invariant, compare strategies, and defend a cost/evidence boundary.

phases.title: Durable software and shared data
phases.premise: Local algorithms become useful when contracts, tests, artifacts, and transactions preserve meaning over time.
phases.gate: Trace a claim through an interface, test, and data boundary; diagnose one failed change; defend a repair with regression evidence.

phases.title: Execution, numerical models, and evidence
phases.premise: Machine behavior, linear structure, continuous change, uncertainty, and optimization explain what a numerical or ML claim can mean.
phases.gate: Derive a projection or likelihood step, name a numerical/data assumption, reject an overclaim, and explain what evidence would change it.

phases.title: Machine, network, and runtime boundaries
phases.premise: Applications live inside machines, processes, schedules, networks, and trust boundaries; each changes what can be known.
phases.gate: Read a trace across system layers, name an ownership/failure boundary, and reject a claim the observation cannot establish.

phases.title: Formal theory, classical AI, and learning
phases.premise: AI joins language, search, decision, representation, statistics, execution limits, and evidence rather than a single model call.
phases.gate: Model a problem before selecting an algorithm or model; identify an assumption, data boundary, and transfer risk.

phases.title: Evidence and human control
phases.premise: A model or agent is useful only when its assumptions, authority, feedback, and uncertainty remain inspectable and challengeable.
phases.gate: Produce an evidence-and-human-control packet naming the claim, limitation, owner, and next falsifier.

phases.title: Capstone release and oral architecture defense
phases.premise: A maintained release must connect mathematical argument, implementation evidence, tests, security, human impact, and revisable decisions.
phases.gate: Defend a versioned evidence bundle: claim, trace, test/observation, human impact, limitation, rollback, and next reason to revise.
